newsitem.title: singapore: Asian crude weakens, W. African losing attraction.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude weakens, W. African losing attraction.

text.p: Asian crude prices were lower on Wednesday, pressured by falling global futures values, as regional trading of Indonesia grades picked up.
Minas was heard trading at ICP +15 cents per barrel for 150,000 barrels between a U.S. major and a Japanese trader, with the same refinery buying a second parcel of 100,000 barrels at the same price.
Many players remained sidelined ahead of the Indonesian export allocations from Pertamina, but they said they expected a firmer market for June loading barrels.
The Brent/Dubai was on widening trend and Brent was forming backwardation, making West African grades less attractive.
China, which has been a major buyer of Cabinda over the past two months, was now expected to find the economics of rival crudes Minas, Widuri and Cinta more economical.
Duri meanwhile was heard traded at flat for 100,000 barrels between Japanese refiners, confirming a firmer tone for the crude supported by fuel oil blenders.
Two Ardjuna deals were also done in parcels of 100,000 barrels and 150,000 barrels by an equity producer to a trader and an Australian refiner respectively.
The trader was heard swapping the crude for LSWR from Pertamina.
Elsewhere, South Korea purchased two VLCCs of West African crude for loading in June. The first was a VLCC of Bonny Light and Bonny Medium, and the second a combination of Cabinda, Nemba and N'Kossa.
Al Shaheen was said traded by QGPC to a U.S. major at Dubai quotes less 45 cents.
In early London dealings June Brent was last traded at $19.26, down 36 cents on the day after bearish API data.
